title: Pointed affine scheme devissage data without support-dimension equalities
statement:
Let $f:X\to B$ be a locally finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $\mathcal F$ a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and $x\in X$ with $b=f(x)$. The following auxiliary terminology is used. An elementary etale pointed map $(U,u)\to(V,v)$ is an etale morphism $h:U\to V$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] with $h(u)=v$ inducing an isomorphism $\kappa(v)\to\kappa(u)$ of residue fields [def-weil-residue-field]. A pointed affine one-step datum for $(\mathcal F,X,B,x,b)$ consists of affine schemes $X,B,Z,Y$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $B$-maps $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $\pi:Z\to Y$, a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal G$, points $z\in Z$, $y\in Y$, an integer $d\geq0$, and an isomorphism $i_*\mathcal G\cong\mathcal F$. Here $i$ is a closed immersion of finite presentation [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], $\pi$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], $Y\to B$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] with geometrically irreducible fibres [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] all of dimension $d$ [def-kun-dimension], $i(z)=x$, $\pi(z)=y$, $y$ lies over $b$, $\pi^{-1}(y)=\{z\}$, and $\kappa(y)/\kappa(b)$ is purely transcendental [def-trf-purely-transcendental-extension]. For a morphism $h:T\to W$ and an $\mathcal O_T$-module $\mathcal H$, pushforward means $(h_*\mathcal H)(V)=\mathcal H(h^{-1}V)$ for opens $V\subseteq W$, with the $\mathcal O_W(V)$-action induced by the structure-sheaf map of $h$. No equality between $d$ and the dimension of the support of $\mathcal F_b$ is required in this auxiliary notion.

A pointed affine devissage chain for these data is a finite list of such one-step data $(Z_j,Y_j,i_j,\pi_j,\mathcal G_j,z_j,y_j,d_j)$ and maps $\alpha_j:\mathcal O_{Y_j}^{\oplus r_j}\to\pi_{j,*}\mathcal G_j$, $r_j\geq0$, for $1\leq j\leq n$. The first datum is for $(\mathcal F,X,B,x,b)$. Write $\mathcal Q_j=\operatorname{coker}(\alpha_j)$, the quotient sheaf by the image subsheaf (equivalently, the sheafification of the presheaf $V\mapsto (\pi_{j,*}\mathcal G_j)(V)/\operatorname{im}(\alpha_j(V))$). For $j>1$ the datum is for $(\mathcal Q_{j-1},Y_{j-1},B,y_{j-1},b)$. Writing $(Y_j)_b=Y_j\times_B\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(b)$, let $\xi_j$ denote its unique generic point [def-sc-generic-point], viewed in $Y_j$; the map induced by $\alpha_j$ on the residue-field vector space at $\xi_j$ is an isomorphism. Finally $\mathcal Q_n=0$. A chain of length zero is permitted exactly when $\mathcal F=0$ and $X,B$ are affine. Here the residue-field vector space of a module $\mathcal H$ at $\xi$ is $\mathcal H_\xi\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,\xi}}\kappa(\xi)$; stalks and tensor products mean [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Here $\mathcal O_Y^{\oplus r}$ denotes the finite direct sum of $r$ copies of $\mathcal O_Y$, including the zero sheaf for $r=0$. On an affine scheme $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$, a principal affine open means $D(a)=\{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}A:a\notin\mathfrak p\}$ for $a\in A$. A standard shrinking of one datum or a chain means restriction to principal affine opens of the base, its initial scheme, and each $Z_j,Y_j$, containing all marked points, for which the restricted maps, modules, isomorphisms and $\alpha_j$ still satisfy all the displayed conditions. Pullbacks and fibre products mean [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pc-fibre-product].

Retained its intentional omission of support-dimension equalities and its explicit length-zero convention. All component notions already have nodes or inline definitions. Added the existing generic-point definition dependency, and clarified pointed maps, the pushforward scalar action, quotient sheaves, finite direct sums, fibres and principal opens.
